strengths: The paper addresses a meaningful failure mode in visual recognition: avoiding spurious correlations does not ensure robustness when a useful invariant cue becomes unavailable. H-CMNIST provides a controlled diagnostic, with ASGDRO improving shape-only accuracy from GDRO's 61.44% to 69.17%.

The empirical evaluation is broad, spanning subpopulation shifts, WILDS, and DomainBed. Reported improvements over GDRO include worst-group accuracy increases from 90.6% to 91.4% on Waterbirds and from 87.2% to 91.0% on CelebA. These results support the optimizer's practical usefulness.

ASGDRO combines established optimization components in a straightforward, architecture-independent method. Its integration with DPLCLIP improves average DomainBed accuracy from 72.6% to 74.0%, compared with 72.9% for DPLCLIP plus GDRO, supporting its applicability beyond conventional supervised classifiers.

The motivation is clear, and the manuscript provides useful reproducibility material: pseudocode, a code link, hyperparameter ranges, model-selection descriptions, and results across three random seeds for several experiments.
weaknesses: Theorem 1 does not establish its central claim. Under Appendix A.4's model, Z=(1,...,1), θ=λ, and the coefficients sum to one. Taking Y=1 gives zero unperturbed loss, while the exact worst-case squared loss under the stated Euclidean perturbation is ρ²p/2 for every λ. Consequently, a single-feature solution and the uniform mixture have identical objectives. The proof introduces a λ-dependent gradient weighting without justification; the adaptive normalization introduced later is absent from this theorem. This invalidates the claimed theoretical preference for diverse invariant mechanisms and is a principal reason for my weak-reject recommendation despite the empirical merits.

Other steps connecting SIL to parameter flatness require unsupported assumptions. Section 3.2 claims that conditional invariance given the full feature set extends to every subset, which does not follow from Definition 1. Section 3.3 equates the maximum risk over finitely many invariant mechanisms with the maximum over an entire parameter ball; containment provides only an inequality. Likewise, low risk along interpolation paths does not establish low risk throughout that ball. These gaps affect the mathematical foundation of the proposed framework.

The implemented optimizer differs materially from the analyzed objective. Equation (3) and Algorithm 1 use separate adversarial perturbations for each environment, whereas Section 3.5 uses one perturbation derived from empirical risk in every non-toy experiment. Environment gradients can oppose one another, so this shared direction need not expose each environment's sharp directions. There is no direct ablation or approximation analysis establishing that the practical variant retains the proposed mechanism.

The experiments support general robustness improvements more convincingly than the specific claim of achieving SIL. H-CMNIST is the only direct intervention on a known invariant feature, and ASGDRO still drops from 99.83% to 69.17% when color is removed in the setting without the spurious cue. Grad-CAM coverage and lower Hessian eigenvalues do not establish that multiple distinct invariant cues drive predictions. The absence of corresponding interventions on real images or comparisons with rich-feature methods on H-CMNIST leaves the mechanism insufficiently isolated, particularly given the cited prior work on SAM and balanced feature learning.

There are secondary reporting issues: ASGDRO's RxRx1 accuracy is 32.2±0.2% in Table 3 but 30.5±0.1% in Figure 7, without an explanation. Section 4.3 also points to appendix efficiency and sensitivity analyses that are not actually presented as measured results. These issues reduce clarity and reproducibility, although they are less consequential than the theoretical and implementation gaps.
